title: for loops and counting
subtitle: A for loop repeats an operation with a new value each time.
concept: A for loop repeats an operation with a new value each time.
intuition: Call numbers 1, 2, and 3 without writing the same instruction three times.
objectives: Set stop one beyond the last number

body.title: Print a sequence of numbers
body.text: for number in range(1, 4): gives number the values 1, 2, and 3 in turn. range produces integers: it includes 1 but excludes 4. The indented print(number) runs once per value, producing three lines.

body.title: Set stop one beyond the last number
body.text: To count through 5, write range(1, 6). With one argument, range(3) starts at 0 and produces 0, 1, 2. Here we use an explicit start and stop. After the loop, execution continues with the next unindented statement.

body.title: Build a running total
body.text: To add 1 + 2 + 3, start with total = 0 and add each number. The running total changes from 0 to 1 to 3 to 6. Place print(total) outside the loop to print only the final total.

formalDefinition.text: A for loop repeats over items. range(start, stop) starts at start and ends before stop.
conditions: The stop value is excluded. Here the bounds are integers and the step is +1.

derivation.text: number takes the next value each time.
The indented print runs once per value.

interactiveVisual.prediction: The sum from 1 through 3 is 6. What happens if you include 4?
interactiveVisual.caption: Choose an input and predict the result, then select Next step. The arrow marks the next statement to execute; the side panel shows current variables and output produced so far.

experiment.code:
end = 3
total = 0
for number in range(1, end + 1):
    total = total + number
print(total)

interactiveVisual.followUp: Choose 0. Does the loop body run?

workedExamples.title: Count through 3
steps: number takes the next value each time.
The indented print runs once per value.

workedExamples.title: Add the first three numbers
workedExamples.problem: Add 1, 2, and 3 one at a time.
steps: After each addition, total is 1, 3, then 6.
Print the final 6 outside the loop.

answer.code:
total = 0
for number in range(1, 4):
    total = total + number
print(total)

commonMistakes.correction: The stop is excluded, so the values are 1, 2, 3.

commonMistakes.claim: Reset total to 0 on every iteration.
commonMistakes.correction: Initialize total before the loop. Inside it, add to the previous total.

answer.code:

for number in range(1, 5):

print(total)

practice.problem: How many times does range(1, 1) run the loop body?
practice.hint: The start has already reached the excluded stop.
solution: The print outside the loop still runs.

answer.code:
total = 0
for number in range(1, 1):
    total = total + number
print(total)

learningCheck.question: Which numbers are in range(1, 4)?
feedback: The start here is explicitly 1, not 0.
